title: Starting to serenade, Frank Wagner and learning
summary: Began serenading in 1922, picked up lessons informally, and played with guitarist Frank Wagner, whose suicide he describes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, now you yourself, when did you start serenading?
Well, I started serenading back around in 19, let me see, 1922.

Well, I used to fool around a musician, they taught me a few things. Fester Monette crossed the river. And I used to be with one of the best guitar players in town, they called him Frank Wagner. He hung himself. He was working on the P.W.A., things got rough around there and he couldn't support his mother like he wanted, so he just tied a rope around his neck. And he got, stood on a box, tied a rope around his neck and kicked the box from under him. And he fell on his neck and hung himself right uptown there. He was one of the swell guitar players, he used to pick all them nice marches and all that. That's right, I used to play with him. There you go. Well, Frank Wagner used to live on sixth, let me see, he lived on sixth street between Howard, let me see, sixth street between Howard and Liberty. That's where he used to live. In fact, I believe that's why he hung himself. I see. Did he play with bands? Well, the most time he played two, three pieces, mandolin, ukulele and guitar. Sometime a bass guitar and ukulele. I used to play with him. We used to go all around, you know, and all around the French market and all down on Decatur Street and uptown, Auschannel, all around. We used to go around and play, you know. That's way back in, oh, I'd say around 21 and 22, up in there.
